review.raw_markdown:
--- # Walker Miles — Skechers.com Journey Review ### Date: April 14, 2026 | Yesterday's Score: 3/10 --- ## 1. Executive Summary Another frustrating trip. The Men's navigation actually impressed me this time — they've got "Hands Free Slip-ins" right there as a quick link in the menu, which is exactly what I'm looking for. And the product page looked sharp. But then the wheels came off completely: the cart page was a **blank white screen**. Nothing. Just white. That's not a minor glitch, that's a wall between me and my wallet. Search still shoves Women's shoes in my face first. And the site keeps acting like I'm not a Plus member even though I logged in. Two steps forward, one giant step into a void. --- ## 2. Business Impact Score: **4/10** Up one point from yesterday. The Men's navigation and product presentation are genuinely better. But a blank cart page is a conversion killer — no amount of good product pages matter if the checkout path doesn't load. --- ## 3. What's Working **Men's Category Navigation (Step 4)** — Clean, readable list. Large enough text. "Hands Free Slip-ins" is right there as a quick-tap shortcut at the bottom, alongside Wide Fit and Extra Wide Fit. I didn't have to dig around. That's the best screen of the entire journey. **Hands Free Slip-ins Category Page (Step 5)** — Landed exactly where I wanted. Clear heading, 262 results, filter buttons for Wide/Extra Wide/Medium fit. Good explanation of the Heel Pillow technology. Relevant and reassuring. **Product Page (Step 6)** — Solid. Max Cushioning Glide-Step, $115, five stars, 65 reviews, BOGO 50% deal clearly called out, the Hands-Free Slip-Ins badge right on the page. Big images, left/right swipe for more views. I felt good about this shoe. **BOGO 50% Deal Visibility** — Consistently shown top-of-screen across every page. I noticed it. As a price-conscious guy, this matters. **ADD TO CART Button (Step 7)** — Big, blue, full-width. Easy to tap. No complaints there. --- ## 4. What's Weak **Cart Page is a Blank White Screen (Step 8)** — This is the biggest problem on the entire site. After going through the whole journey, finding my shoe, selecting my size — I get a completely empty white page. No items, no totals, no checkout button. Nothing. If I were a real customer, I would have called my daughter to complain and then gone to Zappos. This is a critical failure. **Login Had No Confirmation (Step 3)** — The login step looks identical to the homepage. No "Welcome back, Walker." No name, no account recognition. The cart even shows "0" in the badge. If I logged in, the site didn't bother to tell me. **Skechers Plus Upsell Showing to an Existing Member (Steps 7, 2)** — Step 7 still shows "Join for Free Shipping, Free Returns" even though I'm already a Plus member. Step 2 shows "Free Shipping with Skechers Plus — Join Now for free." I already joined. Stop asking me to join. This is a personalization failure that erodes trust. **Homepage Is All Mother's Day, Zero Men's Content (Steps 1–3)** — The hero image is a mother and daughter in pink shoes. The sub-banner says "Get Mom a Gift She'll Love!" There's nothing for me on the front page. A 62-year-old man who just logged into his account sees zero content relevant to him. No "Welcome back," no men's picks, no comfort tech call-out. **Search Returns Women's Results First (Step 9)** — I searched "slip in." Got 1,012 results. The first two products I see are both Women's — Arch Fit Arcade and Contour Foam Cozy Fit, both labeled "Women's." I'm logged in. The site knows I'm a man. Why is it showing me women's shoes first? **Size Grid Has a Gap (Step 7)** — The size options shown jump from 8.0 straight to 10.5. Sizes 9.0, 9.5, and 10.0 are missing from view. Could be a scroll/cut-off issue, but it's confusing at first glance and could cause someone to think their size isn't available. --- ## 5. Recommendations 1. **Fix the cart page immediately.** A blank white cart is a zero-revenue screen. This is the top priority. Investigate whether it's a login session issue or a rendering failure. 2. **Suppress the Plus upsell for active Plus members.** If I'm logged into a Plus account, replace "Join Now" with "You have free shipping" or a member benefit reminder. This is a quick personalization win. 3. **Personalize the homepage for logged-in users.** Even a simple "Welcome back, Walker — check out Men's Slip-ins" banner would dramatically improve the experience. The Mother's Day hero is fine for non-logged-in visitors, but logged-in members deserve relevant content. 4. **Filter search results by the logged-in user's gender preference.** When a male customer searches "slip in," men's styles should appear first. This is basic merchandising. 5. **Make the login confirmation visible.** Show the user's name or a "Signed in" state after login. The current experience leaves me wondering if it worked. --- ## 6. Bottom Line The bones are getting better. I can navigate to my Slip-ins section without too much trouble, the product page is solid, and the deal is clearly communicated. But the cart doesn't load. That's not an inconvenience — that's a broken checkout. Until that's fixed, none of the other improvements matter for actual sales. And the site still doesn't know who I am even after I log in, which makes the whole "Plus member" value proposition feel hollow. Score: **4/10** — one point better than yesterday, but the ceiling is low as long as the cart is broken. --- ## 7. Evidence **Step 1 — Homepage** - Mother's Day hero with woman and daughter in pink shoes dominates the screen - Sub-banner: "Get Mom a Gift She'll Love! Shop Now" - BOGO 50% OFF bar at very top — deal is visible - No men's content, no comfort tech, no Slip-ins in any visible element - Not personalized — same experience as any anonymous visitor - Phone usability: Logo, search, account, cart, and MENU icons are reasonably sized. Not hard to navigate the top bar. **Step 2 — Dismiss Popups** - No modal popup was dismissed — the page just shifted the sub-banner to "Free Shipping with Skechers Plus Join Now for free" - This is shown to a logged-in Plus member — a personalization failure - Same Mother's Day hero, same non-men's content **Step 3 — Log In** - Screenshot is identical to the homepage — no login confirmation visible - Cart badge still shows "0" - No name, no welcome message, no account indicator beyond the person icon - I genuinely can't tell if the login worked from this screen **Step 4 — Men's Category** - Clean slide-out menu with clear MEN heading - Categories: Shoes, Shop by Activity, Comfort Technologies, Collections, Collaborations, Clothing & Accessories - Bottom shortcuts: Hands Free Slip-ins, Wide Fit, Extra Wide Fit — excellent - Large text, good line spacing, easy to tap - Best-designed screen in the journey for my use case **Step 5 — Men's Shoes (Hands Free Slip-ins)** - Arrived on the right page — heading says "Hands Free Slip-ins" - Description mentions Heel Pillow technology — relevant reassurance - 262 results, width filter options visible - Filter and Sort controls present - Product thumbnails beginning to load at bottom - Readable, well-organized, relevant **Step 6 — View Product** - Skechers Slip-ins: Max Cushioning Glide-Step - Sapphire - Labeled "Men's" — correct - $115.00 shown clearly - 5 stars, 65 reviews — confidence building - "Buy 1, Get 1 50% OFF! Applied at Cart" — deal is explicit - Skechers Hands-Free Slip-Ins badge on the image - Clean layout, readable without zooming, good image size **Step 7 — Add to Cart** - Size grid visible: 7.0, 7.5, 8.0, 10.5, 11.0, 11.5, 12.0, 13.0, 14.0 - Missing 9.0, 9.5, 10.0 from visible grid — appears cut off or absent - Red "Please select a size" warning shown — means the add was attempted without a size - QTY dropdown defaulted to 1 - Shipping/pickup options shown - Skechers Plus upsell shown to existing Plus member — wrong - ADD TO CART button: large, blue, full-width — good tap target **Step 8 — View Cart** - Complete blank white screen - No cart items, no totals, no checkout button, no error message - Nothing rendered at all - Critical failure — this is a broken page **Step 9 — Search ("slip in")** - 1,012 results — strong catalog depth - First two visible products: both labeled "Women's" - Skechers Slip-ins: Arch Fit Arcade - See Ya There (Women's) - Skechers Slip-ins: Contour Foam - Cozy Fit (Women's) - Logged-in male customer should see Men's results prioritized - BOGO deal banner still at top - "Get Mom a Gift She'll Love!" still in sub-banner — not personalized --- ## Technical Audit ## Technical Summary Site runs on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (Demandware). Bot-protection layer (Kasada/kpsdk) is generating repeated 429s that propagate into both the console and the cart endpoint, causing a measurable TTFB spike at checkout. A third-party style widget (Stylitics) has a broken CORS configuration, silently disabling that feature. The page carries 20+ async third-party scripts per load with at least two duplicate script injections observed. LCP and CLS were not captured, leaving Web Vitals coverage incomplete. --- ## Accessibility 30 axe violations total; severity breakdown by page: **View Product — 4 critical:** - `aria-required-children`: ARIA role present without required child roles (malformed widget markup) - `aria-valid-attr-value`: One or more ARIA attributes have invalid values - `button-name`: Buttons with no discernible text (likely icon-only buttons missing `aria-label`) - `image-alt`: `` elements missing `alt` attributes **View Product — 3 serious:** - `aria-dialog-name`: Modal/dialog missing accessible name - `aria-input-field-name`: ARIA input field missing label - `color-contrast`: Foreground/background contrast below WCAG 2 AA 4.5:1 ratio **Homepage — 1 serious:** - `link-name`: Links with no discernible text (empty anchor tags or icon links without `aria-label`) **Men's Shoes — 1 serious:** - `link-in-text-block`: In-paragraph links distinguished by color only (no underline or other non-color indicator) **Sitewide moderate (recurring):** - `landmark-complementary-is-top-level`: `
` nested inside another landmark rather than direct body child - `landmark-main-is-top-level` / `landmark-no-duplicate-main`: Multiple or nested `
` elements - `landmark-unique`: Duplicate landmark roles without distinguishing labels - `region`: Content outside any landmark region - `heading-order`: Non-sequential heading levels (e.g., h1 → h3) 10 additional violations not listed in the input data. --- ## SEO - `lang="en"` correctly set on ``. - All pages served from the same `https://www.skechers.com/` URL in the HTML samples — canonical differentiation between steps was not captured; cannot confirm canonical tags or hreflang for these paths. - The GTM snippet in Homepage and Log In HTML includes a destination ID `G-1234567890` — this appears to be a placeholder/test value. If shipped to production it would create a ghost GA4 property sending real traffic data to an uncontrolled destination. --- ## Performance | Step | TTFB | LCP | CLS | |---|---|---|---| | Homepage | 34ms | — | — | | Log In | 42ms | — | — | | Men's Category | 42ms | — | — | | Men's Shoes | 34ms | — | — | | View Product | 29ms | — | — | | Add to Cart | 29ms | — | — | | **View Cart** | **168ms** | — | — | | Search | 44ms | — | — | - TTFB is strong across all steps except View Cart (168ms), which correlates directly with the 429 on `GET /cart/` — the server is rate-limiting its own cart endpoint. - LCP and CLS are unrecorded for all steps. Without these, no Core Web Vitals pass/fail determination is possible. - Each page load carries 20+ async third-party scripts: TikTok (2), Pinterest, Facebook, Snapchat, Bing, Reddit, Yahoo (2), Nextdoor, Taboola, Google Tag Manager (3+ destinations), Monetate (2), Bloomreach, Quantum Metric, Impact, Creative CDN, Pulse Insights, WebFontLoader. This represents significant main-thread contention risk on low-end mobile hardware. - **Duplicate script injection detected:** - `tags.creativecdn.com/dhGobFICKSkk6J9nvQPw.js` loaded twice on Men's Category - `s.yimg.com/wi/ytc.js` loaded twice on Homepage and Log In --- ## Mobile Optimization - Custom CSS property `--vh: 6.640000000000001px` is set inline on `` — this is a JS-driven fix for the `100vh` mobile browser-chrome problem. The floating-point precision artifact (`6.640000000000001` vs `6.64`) suggests the calculation `window.innerHeight / 100` is being stored without rounding. While functionally minor, it produces unnecessary DOM attribute churn on every resize/scroll event. - `vice-managed-src` attribute pattern is used as a consent-gate mechanism for several scripts (Pinterest, Facebook, Yahoo, Nextdoor, Taboola, Impact). This is a non-standard attribute and depends on a first-party consent orchestration layer to swap in the real `src` — if that layer fails or is blocked, all gated scripts silently do not load with no fallback. --- ## Console & Network Errors **429 — Kasada bot-protection fingerprinting (5 hits):** ``` https://www.skechers.com/149e9513-01fa-4fb0-aad4-566afd725d1b/2d206a39-8ed7-437e-a3be-862e0f06eea3/fp?x-kpsdk-v=j-1.2.308 ``` The Kasada SDK is polling its own fingerprinting endpoint and being rate-limited. This is an internal loop — the bot-protection service is throttling its own client-side probe. Every 429 here means the SDK retries, adding network overhead and console noise. **429 — Cart endpoint:** ``` https://www.skechers.com/cart/ ``` The cart page itself is receiving a 429. If this is also Kasada-gated, a failed fingerprint challenge is blocking cart rendering — directly causing the 168ms TTFB regression and potentially blocking add-to-cart completion for affected sessions. **CORS — Stylitics widget (2 errors):** ``` Access to CSS stylesheet at 'https://web-assets.stylitics.com/style.css?...' blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header Access to XMLHttpRequest at same URL blocked by CORS policy ``` The Stylitics hotspot/theme widget is making a cross-origin CSS fetch that `stylitics.com` does not permit from `skechers.com`. Both the stylesheet load and the XHR fallback fail. The widget renders without its styles. --- ## Recommendations 1. **Kasada 429s (critical):** Coordinate with the Kasada integration team — the `/fp` endpoint is returning 429 to legitimate browser sessions, which cascades to the cart endpoint. Investigate whether the kpsdk version (`j-1.2.308`) has a known polling-frequency bug or whether a rate-limit configuration on the Skechers origin is misconfigured. 2. **Cart 429 (critical):** Isolate whether `GET /cart/` is behind the same Kasada challenge. If a failed challenge blocks the cart response, affected users cannot complete checkout. Add session-level monitoring for 429 rates on `/cart/`. 3. **View Product accessibility — 4 critical violations:** Audit the product page component for: (a) icon buttons missing `aria-label`, (b) `` tags missing `alt`, (c) broken ARIA widget structure. These are WCAG 2.1 Level A failures with legal exposure under ADA/Section 508. 4. **Stylitics CORS:** Either (a) have Stylitics add `skechers.com` to their `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` allowlist, or (b) proxy the stylesheet request through the Skechers origin. The current failure silently breaks the widget. 5. **Remove/fix placeholder GTM ID `G-1234567890`:** Audit GTM container configuration. This ID should not appear in production HTML. 6. **Deduplicate third-party scripts:** Remove the duplicate `creativecdn.com` and Yahoo `ytc.js` injections. Audit the tag manager configuration for the duplication root cause. 7. **Round `--vh` value:** Apply `Math.round(window.innerHeight / 100 * 10000) / 10000` or equivalent to prevent floating-point noise in DOM attribute updates. 8. **Capture LCP and CLS:** The Web Vitals instrumentation is not returning LCP or CLS for any step. These are Google ranking signals and the primary UX health indicators — their absence means the current monitoring is incomplete.
